Using this configuration, the system was calibrated using the cp20-175mmx140mm calibration panel, which resulted in a calibrated measurement volume of 145 mm long, 125 mm wide, and 105 mm deep. Where the long edge of the volume was parallel with the tensile axis of the tensile specimen and the center of the volume coincided with the midpoint of the tensile gauge region. The calibration deviation (epipolar error) was 0.026 pixels and minimum displacement sensitivity was 0.002 mm. Further the region of interest (ROI) was defined as gauge area of the tensile specimen. A random speckle pattern was applied to the gauge region of the specimens prior to testing. This was done by first masking the specimens, then spraying painting them with a flat white spray paint, 8 following by applying a black speckles using flat black spray paint, removing mask so that the ROI was covered in a random speckle patter. During tensile testing multiple image capture rates were used. This was done to minimize the number of saved images to facilitate speedier post processing while not compromising on accurate characterization of the elastic, initial yield and fracture portions of the stress strain curve. During tensile testing of the T4 specimens a fixed frame rate of 9 Hz was used to capture elastic and initial yield behavior. After 90 images were captured, the image capture rate reduced to 5 Hz with a 50-frame ring buffer. This means that at any given point after the post yield phase only the last 50 images were saved at a 5 Hz frame rate, while frames prior to the last 50 images were saved at a reduced frame rate of 1/3 Hz. The T6 specimens used a similar image capture regime. However for the T6 specimens a 7 Hz frame rate was used for the elastic and initial yield portion up to 170 images. After 170 images were captured, frame rate switched to x Hz with a 50 frame ring buffer where images older than the last 50 were saved at x Hz. Collected DIC images were processed using a facet size of 21 pixels and a point distance of 9 pixels. Facet matching was done against the previous stage for the collected image sequence. The center of the facets corresponded to nodes of a triangular mesh. The full 3D displacement field was then measured throughout the test. Strain was computed from the displacement measuremetns. Stress-strain curves were generated where strain was defined as average major strain in the ROI (gauge region) at each image index. Fig. 8. The tensile sample geometry for AA6111 alloy H2-T6.
